subject: What Changed to Your Credit Card Today? Edition 4
summary: Kotak Mahindra Bank pulled the fuel surcharge waiver off four cards on the same day: the Corporate Platinum, Corporate Wealth Signature, Solitaire Business, and flagship Solitaire credit cards.
body_html:
What Changed to Your Credit Card Today?

Edition 4, 22 August 2026

If you're the kind of person who fuels up on your corporate card and never once checks the statement line for a surcharge, today's edition is for you specifically. Kotak Mahindra Bank quietly pulled the fuel surcharge waiver off four of its cards on the same day, three corporate and business cards and its flagship Solitaire card. None of this made a press release. It showed up as one small "removed" line in the fine print, which is exactly the kind of change that costs you money precisely because you're not supposed to notice it.

Kotak Corporate Platinum Credit Card

The card used to waive 1% of the fuel surcharge on every transaction between ₹500 and ₹3,000, capped at ₹3,500 a year. That line is gone now.

Here's what that was actually worth to you. Say you fill up ₹2,500 in fuel four times a month, a fairly ordinary pattern for someone driving a personal or company vehicle regularly. At 1%, the waiver saved you ₹25 a fill, ₹100 a month, about ₹1,200 a year. If you fuel up more often or run a small fleet through this card, you could have been getting closer to the full ₹3,500 cap. Either way, that money isn't coming back from the bank now. It shows up as a surcharge line on your next fuel bill instead.

The catch: petrol pumps charge this surcharge regardless of which bank issues your card, it's Kotak's waiver that disappeared, not a new charge invented out of nowhere. So the honest read is that Kotak just stopped absorbing a cost it used to absorb for you.

Kotak Corporate Wealth Signature Credit Card

Same removal, same terms. This card carried the identical waiver, 1% back on fuel transactions between ₹500 and ₹3,000, up to ₹3,500 a year, and it's been pulled in the exact same update.

Since the math is identical to the Corporate Platinum above, I won't repeat it twice, just apply the same ₹1,200 to ₹3,500 a year range to your own fuel spend on this card. If you're a heavier corporate fuel spender, this is the one where the loss actually adds up to real money over a year, not pocket change.

The catch here is the same one worth repeating: this wasn't a fee hike dressed up as a benefit cut. It's a benefit quietly walking out the door, and your monthly statement is the only place you'll see it happen.

Kotak Solitaire Business Credit Card

This one had a slightly better deal to begin with, and it's the one that lost the most. The waiver here covered 1% of the fuel surcharge across all petrol pumps in India, on transactions between ₹500 and ₹5,000, a wider bracket than the two cards above.

Do the math on a bigger fill. If you top up ₹4,000 in one swipe, the old waiver saved you ₹40. Fill up six times a month, which isn't unusual for a business card covering travel or a small delivery operation, and that's ₹240 a month, roughly ₹2,880 a year, gone. Kotak hasn't republished a fresh annual cap for this specific card alongside the removal, so I can't hand you the exact ceiling the way I could for the two cards above. What I can tell you honestly: the wider ₹500 to ₹5,000 bracket means this card's fuel waiver was worth more per fill than the corporate cards, so its removal likely stings more too.

Kotak Solitaire Credit Card

The same fuel surcharge waiver line was pulled from Kotak's flagship Solitaire card as well, in the same update as the three business and corporate cards above. This is the fourth card losing the same benefit on the same day, which tells you this wasn't a one-off correction on a single product page, it's a lineup-wide call.

Here's where I have to be honest about the limits of what I can tell you: Kotak hasn't republished the exact rupee bracket or annual cap for this card's fuel waiver alongside the removal the way it did for the corporate cards. I'm not going to invent numbers to make this section look more complete than it is. What's certain is the benefit is gone. If you carry this card and fuel up regularly, check your next statement for a surcharge line, and pull up the card's terms and conditions page directly if you want the exact figures Kotak used to publish here.

What I'd actually do with this

If you hold any of these four Kotak cards and you fuel up more than once or twice a month, don't wait for your next statement to find out how much this costs you, check it now. Look at your last fuel transaction and see if a surcharge line has appeared that wasn't there before.

If the number stings, here's a genuinely free fix available to you today: pay for fuel with UPI instead of your card wherever the pump accepts it. Fuel surcharges are a card-network mechanism, they don't apply to UPI payments at all. You lose the reward points or cashback your card might have earned on that spend, but you also lose the surcharge that just came back, so weigh the two against each other for your specific card before you switch every fill-up over.

If you're on the Corporate Platinum or Corporate Wealth Signature and your fuel spend is modest, honestly, this is a real loss but not a card-cancelling one. It's closer to ₹1,000 to ₹3,500 a year depending on how much you drive, worth noticing, not worth panicking over.

The fine print

This is my honest read, not formal financial advice. I'm not your advisor, and before you act on anything tied to your own cards, especially a benefit removal like this one, check your bank's official notification and your card's current terms and conditions page. But here's exactly how I'd think about it.

Monzy
